title: Prompt Sets, Benchmarks, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Samantha Lee
summary: Consolidated playbook describing standards and processes for prompt set creation, benchmark design, model onboarding checks, quantization profile validation, and regression triage. Intended for applied ML engineers, evaluation owners, and platform SREs responsible for guarding model quality during onboarding and runtime changes.
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the standards, templates, and operational procedures for: (1) creating and curating prompt sets, (2) designing and running benchmarks, (3) onboarding models into Redwood serving, (4) validating quantization profiles, and (5) triaging regressions detected by our eval harness. The goal is to provide repeatable, inspectable steps that minimize quality regressions while enabling cost and latency optimizations.

Scope

Applies to: open and fine-tuned models onboarded to Redwood inference (hosted, dedicated, private). Covers both pre-production onboarding and post-deploy continuous monitoring and regression triage. Does NOT replace per-customer compliance or internal security reviews for private deployments.

Owners and Roles

- Author / Maintainer: Applied ML Evaluations team (contact: sam.lee@redwood-inference.internal)
- Primary Reviewer: Model Onboarding team
- Secondary Reviewer: Platform SREs (for performance-related benchmarks)
- Runbook Escalation: Oncall for applied-ml-evals -> eng-sre pager escalation if incident severity >= Sev2

Standards for Prompt Sets

1) Purpose and taxonomy: each prompt set must include an explicit purpose (e.g., "customer support summarization", "code assistant instruction-following"), intended distribution (length, role tokens), and expected failure modes.

2) Composition:
- Minimum size: 200 prompts for narrow domain sets; 500+ for broad benchmarks.
- Sources: curated mix of synthetic, anonymized customer artifacts, and public benchmarks. All customer-derived prompts must be scrubbed and approved by data governance.
- Metadata per prompt: id, source_type, difficulty_tag, expected_output_snippet (optional), seed/variant notes.

3) Template and format: store prompts as newline-delimited JSONL for the eval harness with the following fields encoded in the prompt metadata string: PROMPT_ID | INTENT | INPUT_TEXT | EXPECTED_CRITERIA. Example line: {"prompt_id": "ps-2026-001", "intent": "summarization", "input": "<transcript text>"} (Note: prompt files themselves live in the prompt-sets catalog repo; this doc gives the canonical formatting).

4) Coverage and slicing: define slices for length, entity density, language style, and safety attributes. Each prompt set must include at least three slices that the model owner considers high-risk.

Benchmark Design and Execution

Principles:
- Measure signal aligned to product-level success metrics, not just token-level loss.
- Separate bench types: functional correctness, hallucination/safety, latency/throughput, and cost-per-unit (tokens/embedding units).
- Maintain reproducibility: record model artifact hash, runtime config (batch_size, kv_cache, quantization profile), hardware type, and eval harness commit.

Benchmark run checklist (pre-run):
1. Confirm prompt set and slices are correct versioned artifacts.
2. Lock model artifact (model_id + version + checksum).
3. Capture runtime config: max_seq_len, batch_size, top_k/top_p/temp, streaming enabled flag, quantization profile id.
4. Establish baseline run (golden baseline) for comparison.

Key metrics and thresholds (table shown as text)
\Metric | Measurement | Acceptable threshold (on onboarding) | Monitoring alert threshold (production)
------|-------------|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------
Exact-match / pass-rate | % prompts passing functional criteria | >= 85% for broad sets; >= 92% for narrow domain | drop >= 5 pct from baseline or < 80%
ROUGE / BLEU (where applicable) | score distribution (median) | within 0.05 of baseline median | drop >= 0.07 absolute
Hallucination rate | % prompts with ungrounded claims | <= 3% (customer-facing) | increase >= 2 pct absolute
Latency P50 / P95 | ms per token or per response | P95 <= 1200ms (interactive) | P95 increases by >30% or exceeds SLA
Throughput | tokens/sec or requests/sec | meets target for deployment class | sustained drop >20%
Cost per 1k tokens | USD | Within 20% of baseline (for quantized variants) | sustained increase >30%

Notes: thresholds above are guidance and must be adapted per-product. All baseline runs must include seed and harness commit id for reproducibility.

Model Onboarding Checklist (step-by-step)

1) Pre-onboarding (owner: model-owner):
- Create model onboarding ticket with model_id, training dataset summary, intended use cases, and risk assessment.
- Select canonical prompt sets (functional, safety, and stress tests).
- Run local benchmark suite and record baseline metrics in the model onboarding ticket.

2) Onboarding run (owner: applied-ml-evals):
- Deploy model artifact to staging inference environment with same runtime config intended for production.
- Run the canonical benchmark suite (functional + safety + perf) and compare to baseline.
- Verify quantization profiles (if used) with dedicated validation (see below).
- Produce onboarding report: metrics table, failure analysis, example failures with diagnostics (logprob traces, attention footprint if available), and recommended mitigations.

3) Gate decision:
- Approve for production if functional & safety thresholds pass and performance cost envelope is acceptable.
- Conditional approve if remediation plan is in place and monitored rollout/rollback policy configured (canary + automatic fallback).
- Reject and iterate if regressions exceed defined thresholds.

Quality Guardrails and Automated Checks

- Linting: every prompt set and benchmark config must pass the eval-harness linter (checks for metadata, slice coverage, abusive prompts, and formatting).
- Canary Rollouts: production promotion requires progressive traffic ramp with automatic rollback if P95 latency or hallucination rate exceeds alert thresholds.
- Continuous monitoring: eval harness scheduled runs (nightly for critical prompt sets, weekly for broad sets) and alerting to applied-ml-evals Slack channel and incident system on threshold breaches.

Quantization Profile Validation

Purpose: ensure quantized model variants maintain acceptable quality while reducing cost.

Validation steps:
1) Create quantization profile describing bitwidths per layer, per-tensor vs per-channel, and fallback rules.
2) Run the quantization validation suite: compare quantized artifact to FP16/FP32 baseline across the canonical prompt sets. Record: pass-rate delta, hallucination delta, and latency/cost improvements.
3) Acceptance criteria: functional pass-rate drop <= 3 pct absolute for customer-facing workloads; hallucination increase <= 1 pct absolute; P95 latency reduced or cost per 1k tokens reduced by >= 15% for the quantized profile to be considered operationally useful.
4) If criteria not met, iterate: try mixed-precision, lower aggressiveness, or targeted per-layer exclusions.

Regression Triage Playbook (operational)

Triggering events: nightly eval run alert, customer-reported regression, post-deploy canary alert, or CI model artifact change.

Triage flow (high level):
1) Acknowledge alert in incident system (owner: applied-ml-evals oncall).
2) Collect artifacts: failing prompt IDs, model artifact hashes (current and baseline), runtime config, quantization profile, hardware type, and eval harness commit.
3) Quick classification (10–15 min):
   a) Scope: single-slice vs broad regression.
   b) Severity: Sev3 (single-slice low impact), Sev2 (major customer-facing drop or P95 latency regression), Sev1 (widespread failure or safety-critical hallucinations).
4) Immediate mitigations (depending on severity):
   - Auto-fallback to previous model variant (control plane policy) if configured.
   - Deploy emergency canary rollback for severe regressions.
   - Engage engineering teams: runtime, model-owner, and oncall SREs.
5) Deep investigation (owner: model-owner + applied-ml-evals):
   - Diff outputs for failing prompts; capture token-level probabilities and beam hypothesis lists.
   - Re-run failing prompts on baseline artifact and on a matched runtime but different hardware to rule out hardware regressions.
   - If quantization implicated, re-run with FP baseline or less aggressive profile.
6) Root cause and remediation:
   - Document root cause in postmortem if Sev1/Sev2.
   - For model quality issues, create follow-up items: prompt engineering mitigation, fine-tuning patch, decode parameter adjustments, or prompt-slice-specific guardrails.
   - For infra/perf issues, engage eng-sre and schedule a remediation window.

Escalation matrix:
- Sev3: applied-ml-evals oncall -> triage and fix in next sprint
- Sev2: applied-ml-evals oncall -> model-owner -> eng-sre -> product/PM notified within 2 hours
- Sev1: page eng-sre and model-owner immediately; convene war room; notify leadership and customer success if customer-impacting

Operational artifacts and templates

- Onboarding report template (link to repo): includes metrics table, example failures, diff visualizations, and recommended rollout config.
- Eval harness run command example: eval-harness run --model-id <id> --prompts <path> --commit <sha> --quantize-profile <id> --output <artifact.json>
- Minimum required fields for prompt set manifest: name, description, owner, slices (list), canonical_benchmark_ids (list), linter_version, created_at, last_updated.

Appendix A — Example onboarding approval checklist (short)

- [ ] Onboarding ticket created with artifact checksum
- [ ] Canonical prompt sets selected and versioned
- [ ] Baseline run recorded and attached
- [ ] Quantization validation passed (or N/A)
- [ ] Performance targets (P95, throughput) validated in staging
- [ ] Rollout plan and automatic fallback configured
- [ ] Stakeholders (product, security if needed, eng-sre) notified

Appendix B — Quick diagnostics commands

- Run a focused eval: eval-harness run --model-id m-1234 --prompts prompts/ps-2026-001.jsonl --slices "length>256" --commit <sha>
- Compare outputs: python tools/diff_outputs.py --baseline baseline.json --candidate candidate.json --out diffs.html
